launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.address: 5700 North Eagle Creek Parkway, Indianapolis, IN 46254
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.summary: A 5,300-acre reservoir and forest park with two nature centers, a swimming beach, marina, trails, birding, playgrounds, picnic areas and a canine companion zone.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.hours: Gate hours vary by month: 7:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. in December and January; 7:00 a.m.-6:30 p.m. in November and February; 7:00 a.m.-7:30 p.m. in October and March; 7:00 a.m.-8:30 p.m. in September and April; 7:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. in May; and 7:00 a.m.-9:30 p.m. June through August.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.parking: Vehicle admission includes use of park parking. Enter at 5700 North Eagle Creek Parkway from 56th Street or 7100 North Eagle Creek Parkway from 71st Street, then follow the official park map to the selected facility; the two entrances do not provide equally short approaches to every destination.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.arrival: Choose the destination before entering. The 56th Street entrance is the practical approach for many southern and central facilities, while the 71st Street entrance is closer to the northern nature-center and birding area.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.restrooms: The official map identifies restrooms at developed facilities and picnic areas, with the nature centers providing the most reliable staffed access during their shorter building hours. Remote trails and shoreline areas should not be assumed to have nearby facilities.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.cost: Day admission is $6 per resident vehicle, $8 per nonresident vehicle, $1 per hiker or bicyclist, and $15 per bus. A car-top boat launch is $3 per vessel plus vehicle admission; rentals, reservations, dog-zone access and commercial attractions can cost extra.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.accessibility: The two nature centers and major developed facilities have paved approaches, but wooded trails, shorelines and older recreation areas vary. Indy Parks reports an active accessibility-upgrade project for Pin Oak Trail; verify the route needed before relying on unfinished improvements.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed except inside the Canine Companion Zone. Keep pets away from the swimming beach and wildlife-sensitive areas where posted, and carry out waste.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.family: The nature centers, playgrounds and seasonal beach support very different visits. Confirm center hours, lifeguard presence and weather-dependent operations before promising a particular activity.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.transit: The 2026 IndyGo system map shows service near the 56th Street corridor, but the park is large and internal destinations are widely separated. Check the trip planner for the chosen entrance and expect substantial walking if arriving without a car.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.need: Swim only when lifeguards are present. Bicycles are limited to roadways, boats must follow horsepower and launch rules, and the waterfowl sanctuary prohibits watercraft. Do not leave valuables in vehicles.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.weather: Check National Weather Service Indianapolis forecasts and current Indy Parks notices. Heat, thunderstorms, high wind, ice, snow, reservoir conditions and flooding can independently affect trails, boating, swimming, nature centers and gates.

launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.address: Monon Trail at East 10th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46202
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.summary: Indianapolis's north-south rail trail, running from 10th Street to 96th Street before continuing into Hamilton County and connecting with major greenways, parks and neighborhoods.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.hours: The Monon Trail page does not publish a separate schedule. Indy Parks' system rules state that park hours are dawn to dusk; posted closures, construction and connected-park hours can supersede that general rule.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.parking: There is no single trail parking lot. Choose a legal access point before driving; the operator identifies connections at parks including Frank and Judy O'Bannon Park, Canterbury Park and Marott Park, but each location has its own parking and construction conditions.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.arrival: The Indianapolis segment runs from near East 10th Street to 96th Street. Choose a neighborhood or connection first—downtown/10th Street, Fall Creek, the State Fairgrounds, Canterbury, Broad Ripple or Marott Woods—rather than navigating to one generic midpoint.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.restrooms: The operator does not list trailwide restrooms. Comfort stations or indoor facilities may be available at selected connected parks and businesses, but hours and access vary; do not plan a long trip around an assumed facility.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.cost: Indy Parks lists no admission fee for ordinary Monon Trail use. Parking, transit, food, events and separately operated attractions may charge.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.accessibility: Use the official trail map to choose an access point and review street crossings. The operator does not publish a trailwide accessibility guarantee, and curb cuts, construction, detours and connected-park surfaces can vary by segment.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.dogs: Indy Parks requires dogs to remain on a leash shorter than 20 feet outside designated dog parks. Keep animals controlled around bicycles, runners, crossings and crowded Broad Ripple segments, and remove waste.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.family: The trail can support short family rides and walks, but it is a shared transportation corridor with street crossings and faster users. Choose a short segment near a connected park and supervise children closely.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.transit: IndyGo's 2026 system map shows multiple routes crossing or approaching the Monon, including service around 10th Street, the State Fairgrounds, Broad Ripple and 86th Street. Check the current route page for the selected access point.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.need: The trail connects with Fall Creek Greenway, Central Canal Towpath and the White River trail network. Construction at Canterbury Park is expected through late 2026, so verify current detours and avoid treating every adjacent park as an open trailhead.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.weather: Check National Weather Service Indianapolis forecasts before a long trip. Heat, lightning, high wind, heavy rain, snow and ice can make exposed bridges, shaded pavement and street crossings unsafe even when the corridor is not formally closed.

launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.summary: A historic south-side regional park with a conservatory, formal Sunken Garden, arts center, aquatic center, amphitheater, playgrounds, sports facilities and Pleasant Run Trail connections.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.hours: The outdoor park follows Indy Parks' general dawn-to-dusk schedule. The Conservatory and Sunken Garden are closed Monday, open Tuesday-Saturday 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. and Sunday 1:00-5:00 p.m.; the Arts Center is closed Sunday and Monday and open Tuesday-Saturday 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. by appointment. Other buildings and seasonal facilities keep separate hours.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.parking: Use 2345 Pagoda Drive for the general park. Destination addresses are more useful for the Conservatory and Sunken Garden at 2505 Conservatory Drive and the Arts Center at 2432 Conservatory Drive; parking and approach vary by facility.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.arrival: Choose the destination before driving. Conservatory Drive serves the three evidence-cleared destinations, while the Pagoda, aquatic center, amphitheater and family center occupy other parts of the park and are not interchangeable arrival pins.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.restrooms: Restroom access is most reliable inside staffed facilities during their posted hours. Do not assume an indoor restroom will be open when only the outdoor park is open; seasonal and event facilities can operate independently.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.cost: The Sunken Garden has no admission fee. Conservatory admission is $4 per person; the operator does not post a general park entrance fee. Classes, events, rentals and seasonal facilities may charge separately.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.accessibility: The Conservatory, Sunken Garden and Arts Center have developed approaches, but routes, doors, grades and older outdoor facilities vary. Contact the specific facility before relying on a particular accommodation.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.dogs: Indy Parks requires dogs to remain on a leash shorter than 20 feet outside designated dog parks. Indoor facilities and planted garden areas may post tighter restrictions, so follow destination signs and keep pets away from displays.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.family: The Conservatory, garden, arts programming, playground and seasonal aquatic center serve different ages and schedules. Confirm the exact facility's hours, admission and event requirements before bringing a group.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.transit: The 2026 IndyGo system map shows service around the Garfield Park area. Use the trip planner for the selected Conservatory Drive or Pagoda Drive destination because the park spans several blocks.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.need: The Sunken Garden fountains reopened in June 2026, and a new playground near the Pagoda is scheduled for completion in fall 2026. Treat construction limits and facility schedules as separate from general park access, and check current notices before visiting.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.weather: Check National Weather Service Indianapolis forecasts and current Indy Parks notices. The Sunken Garden closes in inclement weather, and heat, lightning, high wind, snow or ice can affect outdoor facilities and paths independently.

launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.summary: A 95-acre White River park with the landmark Ruins, a staffed nature center, a rebuilt inclusive playground, an arboretum, prairie, gardens and wooded trails.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.hours: Outdoor park grounds are open dawn to dusk. The Nature Center is open Monday-Saturday 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; building access, programs and holiday closures can differ from park hours.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.parking: Free parking is available in three lots: beside the playground, west of the Ruins and near the Nature Center. Select the lot for the destination rather than treating the general Spring Mill Road address as one arrival point.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.arrival: From the south gate, turn right for the playground and left for the Ruins; continue toward the Nature Center lot for the staffed building. Use the exact destination pin for the Ruins or Nature Center.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.restrooms: The Nature Center provides the most reliable staffed restroom access during building hours. The Holliday Park Foundation reports maintained restrooms and drinking fountains near the Ruins, but availability can change with maintenance, events and winter conditions.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.cost: The operator describes free parking and does not post a general admission fee for ordinary park, Ruins, playground or Nature Center visits. Programs, rentals and special events may have separate charges.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.accessibility: The rebuilt playground includes accessible equipment and the developed destinations have paved approaches, but wooded trails, slopes and river-edge terrain vary. Confirm route-specific needs with the park before relying on a trail connection.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.dogs: Indy Parks requires dogs to remain on a leash shorter than 20 feet outside designated dog parks. Follow posted rules at the Nature Center, playground, gardens and wildlife-sensitive areas, and remove waste.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.family: The Nature Center's Habitat Hall and the inclusive playground support family visits, while the Ruins and trails require supervision around masonry, slopes and natural surfaces. Match the visit to building hours and weather.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.transit: The 2026 IndyGo system map shows service in the Spring Mill Road and nearby north-side corridors. Check the current trip planner for 6363 Spring Mill Road and allow for walking between the entrance, lots and selected destination.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.need: The replacement playground opened November 2, 2025. Older playground photographs should not be used to set expectations. The Ruins reopened after revitalization in 2016 and remain an outdoor landmark rather than an indoor building.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.weather: Check National Weather Service Indianapolis forecasts and park notices. Rain, flooding near the White River, heat, lightning, high wind, snow and ice can affect trails, the Ruins and outdoor play even when the Nature Center keeps its normal schedule.

launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.summary: A 1,700-acre urban state park where Fall Creek, forest, paved and natural-surface trails, fishing, picnicking, sledding and former Fort Benjamin Harrison landscapes share one property.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.hours: Indiana DNR describes Fort Harrison as a year-round park but does not publish one current gate schedule on the property page. The Visitor Center is open daily 8:30 a.m.-4:00 p.m.; programs, the museum, inn, golf course and other facilities keep separate schedules.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.parking: Enter the main park at 6000 North Post Road and use the official property map to choose parking for the Visitor Center, Delaware Lake, trailheads, picnic areas or sledding hill. The dog park uses a separate Fall Creek Road entrance and cannot be reached by car through the main gate.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.arrival: Use 6000 North Post Road for the main gate. Choose the intended trail, lake, visitor facility or picnic area before entering because the property is large; the fee-based dog park is isolated north of Fall Creek at 8725 Fall Creek Road.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.restrooms: The official map marks restrooms at developed areas, and recreation buildings include restrooms. The Visitor Center is the most predictable staffed option during its daily 8:30 a.m.-4:00 p.m. schedule; remote trails should not be assumed to have nearby facilities.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.cost: Daily admission is $7 per noncommercial vehicle with Indiana plates, $15 per out-of-state vehicle, or $2 per person age 5 and older arriving on foot or by bicycle. Reservations, the inn, golf and the separately gated dog park can cost extra.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.accessibility: DNR identifies Harrison Trace as an asphalt multi-use trail and says parts are wheelchair accessible, while warning that the route includes hills. Natural-surface trails, wet sections and ravines vary; use the official map and contact the property for a route-specific accommodation.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.dogs: Pets must be attended and kept on a leash no longer than six feet, and ordinary pets are prohibited in public buildings. Off-leash use is limited to the separately gated membership dog park, whose passes and seasonal areas follow their own rules.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.family: The paved Harrison Trace, Visitor Center, picnic areas, fishing access and winter sledding offer different family outings. Match the route to the group's ability, supervise near Fall Creek and ponds, and confirm any staffed or weather-dependent activity before leaving.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.transit: Indiana DNR does not document a park transit stop. Check IndyGo's current trip planner for the 6000 North Post Road gate, and do not assume a route near the former fort reaches the chosen trailhead inside this large property.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.need: The Saddle Barn is temporarily closed in 2026 while DNR seeks a concessionaire. Check the park alert and event pages before traveling for horseback riding, museum access, a program or another separately operated facility.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.weather: Check National Weather Service Indianapolis forecasts and current DNR alerts. Heat, thunderstorms, high wind, flooding, mud, snow and ice can affect Fall Creek, natural-surface trails, fishing and sledding independently.
